newsitem.title: USA: Sequus gets approval of DOXIL in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Sequus gets approval of DOXIL in Australia.

text.p: Sequus Pharmaceuticals Inc said Wednesday the regulatory authorities in Australia and New Zealand have granted marketing clearance for its proprietary anticancer drug, DOXIL.
Sequus said in a press release that the drug will be marketed in these countries by Schering-Plough Corp, its marketing partner, under the trade name CAELYX.

CAELYX is marketed in the United States under the trade name DOXIL for the treatment of Kaposi's sarcoma in people with AIDS whose disease has progressed on prior combination chemotherapy or those who are intolerant to such therapy.
Schering-Plough is currently launching CAELYX in the European Union countries, where it is available in the United Kingdom, Germany, Sweden, Austria, Denmark, Finland and the Netherlands.

Aron Stein, Sequus' Vice President for Regulatory Affairs, said, "Our regulatory people have been working very successfully with the Schering-Plough regulatory personnel to rapidly obtain marketing approval throughout the Schering territory."
Sequus is engaged in the development of proprietary liposome and lipid based products to treat life threatening illnesses.
